title: The Angel

full_text:
Whenever a good child dies, an angel of God comes down from heaven, gathers the sleeping child into his arms, spreads his great white wings, and flies gently over all the places the child loved on earth.

Before soaring to the celestial gates, the angel gathers a large handful of wild flowers to plant in heaven, where they will bloom more radiantly than on earth.

As they flew over green fields and gardens, the angel gathered red roses, blue violets, and white lilies. But flying over a dark, narrow alleyway in the crowded city, the angel descended toward a heap of broken pottery and street refuse in the gutter.

There, lying among the broken shards, lay a dry, withered field marigold that had fallen from a cracked flowerpot.

"Why do you gather that poor, broken flower?" asked the child.

The angel smiled with heavenly tenderness: "In a dark cellar in this narrow lane lived a poor, crippled boy. From his childhood, he lay confined to his bed; on the finest summer days, the sunbeams touched the cellar floor for half an hour, and he would hold his pale hands in the light, saying: 'Today I have been out!'

One spring morning, a neighbor's boy brought him this wild field marigold with its roots intact. The crippled boy planted it in an old cracked earthen pot, watered it with loving care, and watched every leaf unfold. It was his garden, his companion, his little treasure on earth. He smiled at its yellow blossom and smelled its fragrance until the day God called his soul home.

When the boy died, the people cleared the cellar and threw the poor withered marigold into the gutter. But that humble flower brought more pure joy to a suffering soul than the rarest rose in an emperor's palace!"

"How do you know this so well, dear angel?" asked the child with wonder.

The angel looked upon the child with boundless love: "I know it, because I was myself that little crippled boy who lay in the dark cellar, and this was my beloved flower!"

And the angel kissed the child, and they soared together into the golden light of heaven, where the withered marigold bloomed forever in the garden of eternal peace.
moral: The humblest flower cherished in sorrow shines brightest in the garden of heaven.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Angel"?
options: Andersen's tales teach compassion, resilience, and Christian hope
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
